title: The French Blue
subtitle: Some say history turns in an endless loop.

trails.title: Alarms Ringing
trails.description: A city of leisure, the only people that ever seem to be busy are the operators and the police.

content.text:
Hello. Yes, I ... I need to report a missing person.
My Aunt Mary. She's the youngest among the elders in our family ... She's a quiet person. She's always reading poetry we don't really get ... She doesn't drink, and she bakes the best cakes for the kids ... But now she's disappeared. We can't find her anywhere! All her belongings are gone too—her clothes, her books, her baking supplies. Who would take all that with them ...
What does she look like? Oh, sure, she's small and thin, with neat, short brown hair. Ah, and she has a birthmark on her right arm ... No, no, we don't have a photo of her. Yes, we checked every album. I think it's strange too, but there isn't a single picture of her anywhere. She's part of our family, so I don't know why she's not in any of our group photos ...
Wait, what do you mean you can't help? Too many missing people with no proof they exist? What does that even mean?

items.speaker: Vigil Officer
items.text: What did you know about Manus Vindictae at that time?
A stack of photos slides across the table toward Adèle.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: Only that it was some kind of secret society that believed arcanists are superior to ordinary humans.

items.speaker: Vigil Officer
items.text: That's just the surface. They're responsible for so much more.

items.speaker: Vigil Officer
items.text: Fueling conflicts, inciting wars, manipulating minds ... If there's an opportunity to bring chaos, they take it.

items.speaker: Vigil Officer
items.text: Their power extends to all corners of the world in almost every time period, including yours.

items.speaker: Vigil Officer
items.text: The Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn, Acéphale, and what remains of the Rosenkreuzer ... Even Carl Jung and Sigmund Freud were associated with them, whether knowingly or not.

items.speaker: Vigil Officer
items.text: And it looks like you got caught up with them, too. You must've encountered them in Paris.
A black mirror is set down on the desk. Its foggy surface reflecting her face in a blur.

items.speaker: Vigil Officer
items.text: Ms. Tavernier, what you say next is critical. From this moment on, everything you say will be monitored by a lie detector.

items.speaker: Vigil Officer
items.text: Do you consent?

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: I do.
She studies the image of herself while absentmindedly touching the back of her hand.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: You seem confident I've encountered them, but I really have no clue how I would have any connection with them.

items.speaker: Vigil Officer
items.text: Then you've got nothing to worry about.

items.speaker: Vigil Officer
items.text: This is your drawing of the diamond necklace you saw in your dream, correct?
The photos vanish, replaced by a rough pencil sketch.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: Yes.
The fingertip points to the diamond pendant drawn on the paper.

items.speaker: Vigil Officer
items.text: You identified it as the French Blue, correct?

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: I did.
Adèle answers without hesitation.

items.speaker: Vigil Officer
items.text: The French Blue—said to be the most beautiful blue diamond ever. It seems whoever it ends up with meets a horrific end.

items.speaker: Vigil Officer
items.text: First, Louis XIV suffered defeats in his final years, his son was taken by smallpox, and France fell into financial ruin.

items.speaker: Vigil Officer
items.text: Then Madame de Montespan, Nicolas Fouquet, Catherine the Great, George IV of England, and Thomas Hope ... I'm sure you're familiar, Ms. Tavernier.

items.speaker: Vigil Officer
items.text: After all, if it weren't for your ancestors, the diamond would never have come to France in the first place.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: That's true. I grew up hearing all those stories.

items.speaker: Vigil Officer
items.text: Then you must also know that it's impossible for you to be in its possession.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: Of course, sir.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: The French Blue was recut more than a hundred years ago.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: The biggest piece became the Hope Diamond. I doubt it retains even half its former glamor.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: But believe me, at that moment, it was the only conclusion I could reach.
She faces the questioner from her side of the table. The mirror image holds still, untouched by any lie.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: That diamond in my hand could only be the French Blue.
The ticking of the clock rises up over the silence of the room.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Hmm ...

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: You have spent three hours studying that diamond, Adèle.
The jewel expert still feels frozen in place, her head tilted, the diamond in her hand lying forlorn; she is more statue than woman.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: It's real.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Whatever do you mean?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: No sign of forgery. Weighs around 60 ... 70 ... Hmm, let's say 67 carats.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: And it matches the picture in my family's archives.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But how? Is the Hope Diamond a fake? Has the true French Blue always been in the hands of the Taverniers?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: It's impossible. None of it makes any sense. None at all!
She firmly sets it down, her composure breaking as she questions the diviner.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Madame Bouanich, what is the meaning of this? Are you playing tricks on me? Am I seeing illusions because of that cleansing ritual?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: If you insist I arrived with it, then I'm taking it back home!

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Adèle, I run a crystal parlor. I neither sell nor possess any such diamonds.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: I am just as certain as you that I am not its owner.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: This diamond—this French Blue—it doesn't exist. It ... It cannot exist!

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: And yet here it is before you. It has passed every test.
The discussion circles back to where it began. Faced with the proof before her, the jewel expert is left speechless.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I don't understand. Célia gave this to me in my dream. How could it be here in reality? How does something from a dream become real?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Dreams often reveal truths greater than our senses allow us to see.
Beryl remains like an island in a storm, still and unmoving as if the matter were self-evident.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: The material world is a result of contraction, shattering, and reconfiguration of pneuma on its descent through four primary spiritual worlds.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Everything we see is a mere manifestation of its true form. If destroyed in this world, it will yet persist in the spiritual world.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: So long as the idea of it remains, it may return to the world of matter through an Emanation of pneuma.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Perhaps this diamond in your hand is the idea of it manifested for a second time.
The diviner's reasoning is flawless.
But her words only leave Adèle more lost.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But how? All I did was see it in a dream.
She clenches her fist, feeling the pricking of her nails, wondering if this too could be another dream, but all she feels is needless pain.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: So, if this dream made the diamond real, why only it? Why not my friend, Célia? She was there too!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Damn it all! It's like I'm trapped in a dream where you just know something awful is about to happen!
She groans and taps her forehead, tangling herself in the logic.
In the end, a more tangible worry wins out.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: All this is giving me a terrible feeling. I need to find Célia.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: The things she said in that dream ... I have to speak to her before I do anything else.
She presses down on her dragon's head before it can lunge at the diamond—a momentary respite from her growing concern.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Would she be at the campus now? Or still in the field? Maybe I should wait for her at her place?
She lets her eyes wander as she thinks, coming to a sudden realization that there's an answer hanging right in front of her.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Madame Bouanich, you couldn't do a divination to tell me where Célia is now, could you? This diamond came from her, so you can trace it back to her, right?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: I am afraid not. Though it may be a fine material for divination, it will not provide the vision you seek.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: If we are to find your friend, we require an item she has often used or something dear to her.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: No problem! I just—I just need to pick something up from my place. Please, madame, would you wait here for me? I'll be back in 30 minutes at most!
She bolts up from her seat and makes for the door. The diviner smooths her skirt and rises to follow.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: I am sorry, Adèle, but I must close the parlor now.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Ah ...
Her urgency scatters into the air, leaving her with an open mouth searching for the words to fill it.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Then I ...

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: But I am willing to take a little detour on my way home, if I can be of help.
It takes Adèle a moment to process, then she beams, springing to her feet to hold the door open for the diviner. "An even better plan," she reasons.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Thank you! I mean, sorry for taking up your evening. Ah, yes, how much do I owe you for the divination?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Think nothing of it. As I said, the door was opened just for you.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Fate will see to the payment when the time is right.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Wait. So, fate is the one paying you? Not the client? So, what, you work for fate?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: I work for fate?
The driver is startled to see her offhand remark actually made Beryl pause to think.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Hm. I have never heard anyone put it quite like that.
She offers a polite smile as she locks the parlor entrance behind her.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Let's go. Let us see what your friend and my "employer" has in store for us.
